issues.description: The manuscript gives conflicting accounts of when the interventions are administered relative to collaborative recall/misinformation exposure. The Introduction explicitly states the authors decided to place the warning after collaborative recall, but later they state they decided to place all resistance-inducing methods before collaborative recall, while the Procedure actually administers interventions after collaborative recall and just before the final memory test. This inconsistency undermines interpretability and preregistration clarity because timing is central to the theoretical rationale and expected mechanism.
issues.quote: In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall (see the rationale for the research below). ... What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). ... After that, the third phase will take place: it will consist in the procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation ... Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity ... they will complete the individual memory test

issues.description: The analysis plan states both that the individual memory test will be open-ended and that it will also use a two-alternative forced-choice format. These are materially different outcome measures with different psychometric properties, scoring rules, and susceptibility estimates. Because the key dependent variable is inconsistently defined, the planned analyses cannot be meaningfully evaluated.
issues.quote: Immediately after the participants are done with the methods ... they will complete the individual memory test ... The test will contain 20 open-ended questions ... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test ... In existing research using the MORI technique a two-alternative forced-choice questions test was used as the main index of correctness of answers. ... In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.subcategory: mismatch between discussed critical items counts
issues.description: The manuscript inconsistently states the number of critical items discussed during collaborative recall. The collaborative recognition test is said to include four critical details, and all pairs discuss the same set of four details, yet later the within-subject factor compares discussed versus non-discussed items across eight critical details. If only four of eight critical items are discussed, the scoring and ANOVA structure must reflect unequal item subsets; this is not clearly specified and the text oscillates between treating all discussed items as misinformation and all eight critical items as part of the same outcome.
issues.quote: The test will comprise 12 questions, four of which refer to critical details ... In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. ... The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details included in the movie, regardless of whether they were subsequently discussed.

issues.description: The conversion from Hedges' g = 1.13 to Cohen's f = 0.57 for a repeated-measures ANOVA is not justified and appears dubious. Effect size conversion depends on the specific design and parameterization; a simple conversion from standardized mean difference to f without explicit formulas and assumptions is inappropriate. Because sample size is based on this conversion, the power analysis may be inaccurate.
issues.quote: Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13. This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57.

issues.subcategory: meta-analysis based on only two highly heterogeneous studies
issues.description: The pooled effect used for power analysis is derived from only two studies with extremely discrepant effects (g = 1.92 vs. g = 0.38). Estimating a random-effects pooled effect from such sparse and heterogeneous evidence is unstable and provides a weak basis for sample size planning. This is especially problematic because the resulting pooled estimate is then used as if precise.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020). Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.description: Participants are nested within pairs and receive the manipulation at the pair level ('Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned'). However, the planned ANOVA appears to treat individuals as independent observations without accounting for dyadic clustering. Because pair members influence each other during collaborative recall, responses are statistically dependent. Ignoring this violates independence assumptions and can bias standard errors and p-values.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs). ... Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups ... The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels ... and one between-subjects factor with four levels

issues.description: The three intervention conditions are not matched in content, duration, cognitive load, or procedure. Two are 7-minute podcasts, while the DRM condition involves an active memory task, individualized feedback, and then an additional motivational podcast or exhortation. Any differences could reflect arousal, engagement, self-relevance, task interruption, expectancy, or time-on-task rather than the intended mechanism. This threatens internal validity of between-group comparisons.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... First, in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used ... The results will be fed back to participants ... Next, the participants’ motivation to resist memory suggestibility will consist in them listening to a podcast ...

issues.description: Each intervention bundles several mechanisms, making it impossible to determine what construct is being tested. Extended warning includes warning, education, source monitoring guidance, social reassurance, and enlightenment. Demonstration and motivation combines a false-memory induction with motivational and moral messaging. Education about memory includes multiple theories and may alter confidence. Because interventions are multicomponent and overlapping, any observed effect cannot be attributed to the named construct.
issues.quote: the following ideas were included ... a clear warning ... an extensive lecture ... information about the possibility of confusing sources ... information that many people do, in fact, remember the correct content ... an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception. ... Demonstration and motivation ... consists of two elements: (1) directly demonstrating the fallibility of memory ... and (2) motivating them to provide correct answers

issues.subcategory: normative influence ruled out without justification
issues.description: The manuscript claims normative influence is 'completely ruled out' because the final test is individual. This is conceptually overstated. Normative processes may operate during collaborative recall, become internalized, or influence later responding even in private through anticipated evaluation, conflict avoidance habits, or deference. Overstating exclusion of one mechanism weakens the theoretical framing and may lead to misinterpretation of results.
issues.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study

issues.description: The authors make strong claims about mechanisms such as abandoning the consistency assumption, enhanced source monitoring, increased mindfulness, and increased reliance on one's own memory, but they do not measure these mediators. Without process measures, any effect of the interventions cannot be attributed to these proposed mechanisms.
issues.quote: we assumed that the extended warning would cause participants to abandon the consistency assumption, make them more alert to discrepancies ... and consequently cause them to rely on their own knowledge ... We assume that the lecture will also enhance memory monitoring, sense of memory efficacy or even memory-related affect.

issues.description: The manuscript states that pairs will be randomly assigned but gives no details about allocation sequence generation, concealment, blocking/stratification, or implementation. For a controlled experiment, these details are needed to assess selection bias and replicability.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups

issues.description: There is no description of whether experimenters administering interventions, coding discussions, or scoring open-ended responses will be blind to condition. Given open-ended scoring and audio-recorded discussion coding, lack of blinding could introduce expectancy bias.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded. ... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test

issues.description: The manuscript does not define how open-ended responses will be coded as correct, misinformation-consistent, or 'other,' how ambiguous/partial answers will be handled, whether spelling variants are accepted, whether multiple coders will be used, or how inter-rater reliability will be assessed. These omissions prevent evaluation of measurement reliability and reproducibility.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers.

issues.subcategory: discussion coding and manipulation check unspecified
issues.description: Although discussions are audio recorded and misleading information is central to the design, the manuscript does not specify how recordings will be coded, by whom, with what reliability, or whether actual exposure to misinformation will be verified. This is essential because some pairs may not exchange misinformation or may fail to discuss target details effectively.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded. ... In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s differing version of events.

issues.subcategory: misinformation exposure assumed rather than measured
issues.description: The analysis plan classifies all discussed items as containing misinformation regardless of what actually occurred in discussion. This is a serious design and scoring flaw because exposure depends on whether the partner actually voiced discrepant information. Misclassifying non-exposed items as exposed attenuates validity and can distort both the main effect and intervention comparisons.
issues.quote: we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s differing version of events.

issues.description: The manuscript first states that only partner answers inconsistent with the participant's version are misleading and that some discussed items will not be classified as misleading if the partner guessed the participant's version or said 'don't know.' It then states all discussed items will be categorized as having contained misinformation. These statements are incompatible.
issues.quote: All the answers provided by the partner during the discussion ... are misleading ... However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen ... the situation will not be classified as misleading. ... In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation

issues.subcategory: ANOVA inappropriate for bounded count outcomes
issues.description: The primary outcomes are counts out of a small fixed number of items (e.g., number of correct answers among discussed/non-discussed critical details), likely non-normal and bounded. A standard ANOVA on such data may violate distributional assumptions. Mixed-effects logistic/binomial models at the item level or generalized linear mixed models would be more appropriate, especially given nesting within participants and pairs.
issues.quote: The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels

issues.description: The plan proposes analyzing four indices from the open-ended test plus average accuracy on filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions, along with pairwise group comparisons and exploratory analyses, but does not specify a primary outcome or any correction for multiple testing. This inflates Type I error and introduces analytic flexibility.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.description: The manuscript does not clearly specify which dependent variable constitutes the confirmatory test of intervention efficacy. It references accuracy differences, four derived indices, and discussed/non-discussed comparisons. This leaves substantial flexibility in selecting an outcome after seeing the data.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices ... The efficacy of a given method will be confirmed if the magnitude of memory conformity (expressed as the difference between the accuracy on discussed and non-discussed items) is smaller

issues.description: The manuscript mentions follow-up pairwise comparisons if the interaction is significant but does not specify which comparisons are confirmatory, whether tests are one- or two-sided, or how multiplicity will be handled. The phrase 'directional significance tests are assumed' is too vague for a preregistered analysis plan.
issues.quote: For the planned comparisons between two groups, which will be necessary if the general interaction is significant ... Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed. ... In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.description: No plan is provided for handling incomplete item responses, skipped confidence ratings, equipment failures affecting only part of a session, or partially missing discussion data. Simply excluding participants for technical problems does not address ordinary missingness and may bias results.
issues.quote: 3.1. Exclusions We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: Because participants are tested in pairs and discussions generate mutual misinformation, exclusion of one member of a pair may affect the validity of the other member's data. The manuscript does not specify whether exclusions occur at the participant or pair level or how such dependencies will be handled.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs). ... We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: The study does not include checks to verify whether participants understood or engaged with the podcasts, experienced the DRM illusion, or increased motivation/awareness as intended. Without manipulation checks, null effects are uninterpretable and positive effects cannot be linked to the intended intervention content.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... The results will be fed back to participants in order to demonstrate to them that their memory was vulnerable

issues.subcategory: DRM false recall may not index social suggestibility
issues.description: The DRM task induces associative false memory, not co-witness social misinformation susceptibility. Using DRM performance as a predictor of MORI-based memory conformity may have weak construct validity because the paradigms involve different cognitive and social mechanisms.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.subcategory: education intervention may alter confidence opposite to intended construct
issues.description: The authors acknowledge that educating participants about memory fallibility could decrease confidence and potentially increase suggestibility. This means the intervention may not cleanly operationalize 'resistance' or 'metamemory improvement'; it could simultaneously manipulate confidence, anxiety, and response conservatism. The construct being tested is therefore ambiguous.
issues.quote: presenting participants with research confirming the fallibility of memory may result in decreased confidence in their own memory, which, in turn, might result in increased suggestibility.

issues.subcategory: possible contamination within pair during interventions
issues.description: Interventions appear to be delivered to both members of a pair together after they have already discussed the event. The manuscript does not clarify whether pair members receive the same intervention simultaneously, whether they are separated, or whether additional interaction is prevented. If delivered together, social cues or continued conversation could differentially shape effects and compromise individual-level inference.
issues.quote: The participants will be randomly divided into four groups ... Participants in the ‘Extended warning’ group will listen to the podcast ... those in in the ‘Education about memory’ group will listen to the podcast ... Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback

issues.description: The manuscript says discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but later states all pairs will discuss the same four critical details. This leaves unclear what exactly is counterbalanced: item versions, assignment of discussed status across participants, or movie versions. The design cannot be fully evaluated without a clear counterbalancing scheme.
issues.quote: In the study, the memory conformity effect will be measured in a within-subjects design and discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced. ... In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.subcategory: counterbalancing claim conflicts with fixed discussed items
issues.description: Claiming full counterbalancing of discussed versus non-discussed items contradicts the statement that every pair discusses the same four critical details. If the same items are always discussed, item-specific memory differences are confounded with discussed status.
issues.quote: discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced. ... each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.subcategory: item confound between discussed status and item identity
issues.description: Because the same four critical details are discussed by all pairs, discussed status is confounded with item identity unless discussion assignment is counterbalanced across item sets. Any discussed vs. non-discussed difference may partly reflect intrinsic item difficulty rather than misinformation exposure.
issues.quote: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.description: The sample is limited to volunteers aged 16–35 recruited via media/internet advertisements. Findings may not generalize to children, older adults, forensic witnesses, or broader populations with different social dynamics and memory profiles. Yet the discussion repeatedly frames implications broadly for justice systems.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet. ... Due to the serious consequences of inaccurate testimonies, research on methods of reducing the memory conformity effect is extremely important for the proper functioning of justice systems.

issues.description: The MORI technique is said to bring laboratory conditions closer to real life, but the study still uses brief video stimuli, student-like volunteers, short delays, and contrived discussions. Claims about practical preparation of real witnesses may exceed what the design can support.
issues.quote: The main reason for its popularity is the fact that the MORI technique brings laboratory conditions closer to the real-life situations in which witnesses discuss a crime and are then individually interviewed by law enforcement officers. ... In reality, it is most effective to prepare a witness before possible misinformation reaches them.

issues.subcategory: moral/persuasive framing may affect demand characteristics
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition explicitly tells participants that they may testify in court and strongly encourages reliance only on their own memory. This may induce demand characteristics or hypothesis guessing rather than genuine resistance to misinformation, so any effect could reflect compliance with perceived experimental expectations.
issues.quote: The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner.

issues.subcategory: control condition may not be expectancy-matched
issues.description: The control podcast on soft skills related to social attitudes is likely not matched to the experimental conditions on relevance to memory, legal testimony, or self-focused cognitive engagement. Differential expectancy and salience may bias group differences.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The manuscript does not provide the podcast scripts, exact duration, voice, delivery mode, whether headphones are used, or whether participants listen individually or together. These details are necessary for replication and for assessing whether differences across conditions reflect content or presentation.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.subcategory: no handling of suspicion/deception awareness in confirmatory analyses
issues.description: Participants are asked at the end what they think the real purpose was, but the manuscript says these data will be used only for exploratory analyses. Given the heavy use of deception and explicit enlightenment in one condition, awareness could materially affect behavior and should be integrated into confirmatory exclusion/sensitivity analyses.
issues.quote: Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance.

issues.description: Excluding participants for 'any technical problems' is underspecified and leaves room for subjective post hoc decisions. The plan does not define what counts as a technical problem, who decides, or whether exclusions occur before outcome inspection.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.subcategory: no preregistration or Stage 1 deviation handling details
issues.description: Although this appears framed as a registered report/Stage 1 submission, the manuscript does not specify versioned hypotheses, primary analyses, or how deviations from the approved protocol will be documented. Given multiple internal inconsistencies, clear preregistration details are especially necessary.
issues.quote: If the Stage 1 review is accepted, the resubmission should be completed no later than in 2023.

issues.description: The adaptation of inoculation theory from persuasion resistance to eyewitness memory conformity is asserted rather than theoretically established. The mechanisms in persuasion (counterarguing, legitimacy discrimination) are not obviously analogous to source-monitoring in memory. The manuscript does not explain why an inoculation-style DRM demonstration should transfer to social memory contamination specifically.
issues.quote: We adapted the ideas from the research described above in the hope that it may be useful in mitigating memory conformity.

issues.subcategory: confidence ratings planned but not analyzed
issues.description: Participants provide confidence ratings for each answer, but the analysis plan does not specify any confirmatory or exploratory use of these data. This is a missed opportunity because confidence is theoretically central to the rationale and could help distinguish mechanisms such as informational influence versus memory-strength changes.
issues.quote: for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% ... to 100% ...
